why_next: The next question changes the LEVEL OF DESCRIPTION, not the estimator, because this run measured an identifiability limit rather than a signal shortage. The mandate asked whether the change in an HTTP response signature under a perturbed parameter factorizes into a cache part, a site-memory part and a mechanism-semantic residual. The design made that residual a rank-MAGNITUDE prior, because MECHANISM_CONDITIONED emits a distinct value per parameter rank. That choice is what failed, and it failed on the positive control, where the mechanism declarations are true BY CONSTRUCTION and therefore cannot be wrong: the observed signature distance took at most two distinct values across five parameter ranks for M_PAGINATION and exactly one for M_SECTION, while the treatment emitted five rank-ordered values, so a predictor that uses no mechanism, no site, no parameter and no data recovered 87% of the treatment's gain (6.908598 against 7.923085 nats under the executor-added corrected distance) and on the real Web pools it beat the treatment outright (12.102727 against 6.828579 nats). A prior over HOW MUCH a parameter changed a document has no observable counterpart in an HTTP response, which exposes only WHETHER the signature changed. This is a statement about the observable and it is the most reusable thing in the packet: before running another interventional predictor comparison on this substrate, ask whether the treatment's output variable is something the measurement can actually distinguish. The second reason for changing level is that the substrate DOES carry intervention signal, contrary to the inherited expectation: query-parameter perturbation changed the body at constant status in 25.47% of 691 successful probes against an 87.5% byte-identical repeat floor, so the estimand is not empty. What is missing is the ability to separate that signal from host-side drift and template rotation, because the frozen B_SITE_TEMPLATE_MEMORY arm could not be exercised at all (global_mean fallback on 105 of 105 and 870 of 870 test instances) and no arm held the parameter fixed while varying only the instant. The third reason is that the query arm is the only arm that bites: fragments are inert by HTTP definition (88.9% byte-identical in 693 successful probes) and path parameters are largely absent (71 of 905 probes at 2xx/3xx), yet the frozen admission criterion required 12 of 15 probes at 2xx/3xx across all three arms, so the pool could never reach the required 20 sites. The fourth reason is that the previous instrument had three pre-execution-detectable defects, all now quantified, and a repeat without fixing them would be a fourth instance of the same failure rather than a test: the frozen distance assigns 0.3 to identical signatures so the inert test cannot fire; the strong baseline is keyed on the site while the split is at the site so no test site can own a training cell; and the permutation null permutes within an intervention_type that contains exactly one mechanism, so it is non-degenerate (999 distinct values in 1,000 permutations, the inherited placebo repair confirmed a third time) yet centred on the treatment (percentile 0.487). The fifth reason is the control-plane fact this packet discovered: prereg conditions M2 and M3 were unsatisfiable by construction because research/EXPERIMENT_PACKET.md s2 lets DESIGN emit only spec.json and prereg.md and scripts/freeze_experiment.py hard-codes exactly those three digests, so any successor that again writes 'must be hashed into freeze.json' has pre-committed itself to MEASUREMENT_INVALID. The sixth reason is unused capacity: 59 of 80 conditional GETs returned 304, so the cache/revalidation component of the requested factorization was available on this substrate and the frozen protocol issued none of those requests, leaving component (i) at zero information by construction. This is explicitly NOT a fifth certification battery on the same template and NOT a retune of this freeze, which is spent. It is also not the only admissible direction: the registry's other next_gate programs (barriers, timescales, geometry, multiscale dynamics) remain open and are not foreclosed by this verdict, but each requires a substrate with genuine state dynamics, and the unvalidated Chromium CDP browser path must not be assumed, so that choice is a Global Research Director portfolio call recorded in dependencies.

THE FROZEN DISTANCE IS NOT A METRIC, and this single sign accounts for the entire positive-control failure. prereg s6.3 defines d = 0.4*I(status_diff) + 0.3*Jaccard(cache_headers) + 0.2*I(body_sha256_diff) + 0.1*I(structural_hash_diff). The Jaccard term has the wrong sign, so the distance INCREASES with header similarity: an identical signature scores exactly 0.3, which makes the prereg s8.2 inert test ||delta|| < 0.01 unreachable (observed 0.0000 on the 105-instance held-out test set, vacuous) and scores the provably inert fragment arm of the positive control at 0.3, indistinguishable from a real change. With identical ground truth, identical predictors and the identical server, the positive control reads -1.4894969491411805 nats under the frozen formula and 7.923085363078009 nats under 0.3*(1-Jaccard). The indicator terms independently violate the triangle inequality. BOUNDED: this rejects this formulation; the executor did NOT establish that 0.3*(1-Jaccard) is the correct repair, only that it is far better than the frozen form.

THE FROZEN STRONG BASELINE COULD NOT BE EXERCISED. It fell back to the global mean on 105 of 105 frozen-pool test instances and 870 of 870 exploratory test instances. B_CACHE_REVALIDATION emitted exactly 1 distinct value on all 105 frozen-pool test instances. Consequently B_COMBINED_NULL, the reference arm of the primary metric, is effectively one global constant, and the frozen contrast between component (ii) and the treatment was never run: the entire comparison is the treatment against one constant.

BOUNDED SUBSTRATE FACTS, admissible regardless of disposition, bounded to one curated pool and one collection window on one stdlib HTTP client with no JavaScript, no cookies, no sessions and no rendering. (i) Fragment interventions are inert by HTTP definition: conditioned on a 2xx/3xx response, M_ANCHOR was byte-identical to the baseline at the same status in 0.888889 of 693 cases and had the same status in 1.0000 of them, because fragments are not transmitted in a request target. (ii) Query parameters DO produce body variation above the measured noise floor: conditioned on a 2xx/3xx response, M_PAGINATION changed the body at the same status in 0.2547 of 691 cases, against a site-dynamism floor of 0.8750 (140 of 160 repeat fetches of an unchanged URL were byte-identical, with 10 of 80 candidates varying on at least one repeat). This is the first bounded positive substrate result in this lineage and it contradicts the inherited expectation that public HTML documents show no per-intervention variation. (iii) Path parameters are largely absent: M_SECTION returned 2xx/3xx in 71 of 905 probes (0.0785), and 151 candidates returned 404 for all five path values; its apparent signature variation is dominated by 404-versus-200 status differences, i.e. a transport effect, not section selection. (iv) Revalidation is available and was never used: 59 of 80 conditional GETs returned 304 (0.7375) and 21 returned 200, but the frozen collection protocol issues no conditional requests, so component (i) of the requested three-way factorization was unmeasurable by construction. (v) Only the server-visible component of any mechanism is observable here; the declared effect of M_ANCHOR is client-side scrolling, which a stdlib client cannot observe by definition.
